These are the tools an agent sees when it connects to the NextPress MCP server. To set the server up, see [MCP server](/docs/developers/mcp-server).

## Tools

### activate_theme

*Changes content*

Make this theme the one the current site draws with.

### add_docs_page

*Changes content*

Adds a page or a group to a docs. A page holds text; a group is a heading in the sidebar that holds other pages and has no text of its own. Put it under a page or group with parentId, or leave parentId out to put it at the top of the docs. A new page is a draft. Its address is made from its title; change it with update_docs_page. Give mdx to start the page with text, or leave it out and write the text with write_docs_page.

### apply_page_phone_fixes

*Changes content*

Works on one saved page, or on a blog post when content_type is "post". Name it in "id". Repairs the phone-layout problems check_page reports as warnings, wherever there is an obvious fix: a fixed width wider than a phone becomes "width: 100%" with the old width as a maximum, and a box with a max width is told to fill its space. When a block is selected, only that block and what is inside it are fixed. Returns what was changed. Problems with no automatic fix stay; check_page lists them. Run it when a change reply lists phone warnings.

### build_blocks

*Changes content*

Turns block descriptions into ready-made blocks for create_page or create_template_part. A block is \{ name, label?, content?, styles?, children? \}, the same shape change_page_blocks takes: it starts exactly as the editor would insert it, then your content and styles are laid over that. get_block_type lists a block's content fields; other fields are refused. To add to or change a page that already exists, use change_page_blocks instead: it also checks the page.

### change_page_blocks

*Changes content*

Works on one saved page, or on a blog post when content_type is "post". Name it in "id". Change the page: insert, update, delete, move or replace blocks. Send 1 to 50 ops in one call. They run in order and are all-or-nothing: if an op is wrong, or the change would add a problem the server would refuse, nothing changes and the reply says why, so fix it and send the whole call again. Problems the page already had do not block a change; the reply names them.

Ops (each has "op"; ids come from get_page_outline, or are refs made earlier in the same call):
- insert \{ parentId, index?, block \}: add a new block. parentId is a container's id or ref, or null for the page root (at the root, blocks go inside the page shell; an empty page gets its shell automatically). Leave index out to add at the end.
- update \{ id, label?, content?, styles?, fillBehind? \}: change fields of one block. Only the fields you send change; everything else stays. A null value removes that field or style.
- delete \{ id \}: remove a block and everything inside it. The page shell can't be deleted.
- move \{ id, parentId, index? \}: move a block (and what is inside it) to another container, or to the root with null.
- replace \{ id, block \}: swap a block and everything inside it for a new block in the same place.

A block is \{ name, ref?, label?, content?, styles?, fillBehind?, children? \}. The name may leave out "core/" (heading is core/heading). It starts exactly as the editor would insert it (default content, styles and starting children, such as an accordion's first items or a form's fields), then your content and styles are laid over that. Content fields must be ones the block has; get_block_type lists them, and any other field is refused. Children replace the starting children and only containers can have them. A block nests four levels deep in one call (the block plus three levels of children). For a deeper tree, or to add to a block you are making in the same call, give it a ref (such as "hero") and use that ref as parentId in a later op.

Limits: 50 ops and 300 new blocks per call. When the person selected a block, only that block and what is inside it can change; the selected block itself can be updated or replaced but not deleted or moved.

Returns what changed, the new blocks as an outline with their ids (use those ids in later calls; a ref lasts one call), and a check of the page after the change: phone warnings for the blocks you touched, or that the whole page has no problems, so you don't need check_page after a change. Warnings don't block the change; apply_page_phone_fixes fixes them. Work in small steps: one section per call. It saves with the page version it just read. If the page was saved somewhere else in the meantime, nothing is changed and you are told to read the outline again.

### check_page

*Reads only*

Works on one saved page, or on a blog post when content_type is "post". Name it in "id". Checks the whole page and lists every problem. Four kinds: structure (unknown block names, repeated ids, children inside a block that cannot hold any), save (what the server would refuse when saving, such as a bad icon or tag name), placement (one page shell, only at the root), and phone (layouts that overflow or break on a phone). Structure, save and placement problems must be fixed; phone problems are warnings that apply_page_phone_fixes can usually repair. change_page_blocks already checks the page after every change, so use this to review a page you did not just change, or when the person asks for a check.

### copy_brand_logo

*Changes content*

Saves a brand logo from svgl.app into this site's media library and returns the media item; use its url in an image or icon block. Use it for logos of well-known brands (payment providers, tools, social networks) instead of linking to another website. Asking for the same logo again returns the copy already saved. Only logo files on svgl.app are accepted, such as https://svgl.app/library/github.svg.

### create_blog

*Changes content*

Create a blog section. Posts require this blogId.

### create_docs

*Changes content*

Makes a docs on this site. Its home page is created first, empty and as a draft, and it is the top of the sidebar. Give the docs a name. Its address is made from the name unless you pass slug, the first part of the address: docs gives /docs. Returns the docs' id (homeId) for the other docs tools. Check list_docs first, so you do not make a second copy.

### create_page

*Changes content*

Create a page. Defaults to draft so owners can review in the admin CMS. Pass blocks from build_blocks, or create it empty and build it step by step with change_page_blocks (see the build_page prompt).

### create_post

*Changes content*

Create a blog post (defaults to draft). blogId is required.

### create_template_part

*Changes content*

Creates a template part on this site: one layout block (core/group, core/stack, core/columns, core/container, core/header, core/accordion, core/popup, core/form) with anything inside it. Send either blocks (exactly one such block with its children, for example from build_blocks) or rootBlock to start from an empty one; not both. With neither it starts as an empty core/group. Returns the part's id. To show this part on a page, insert a core/template-part block with content \{"templateId": "&lt;id>"\} using change_page_blocks. Creating a part does not change any page.

### create_theme

*Changes content*

Add a theme. It is not the site theme until activate_theme.

### delete_docs_page

*Deletes*

Deletes one docs page or group. A page or group that still has pages under it cannot be deleted: move or delete those first, and the reply says so. Ask the owner first unless they asked for this deletion.

### get_block_type

*Reads only*

Returns one block type in full: label, description, kind, category, where it may sit, the note on when to use it, its content fields (send them under "content" in change_page_blocks; no other field is accepted), and an example block exactly as the editor inserts it (default content, styles and starting children). Use it before you build a block you have not used yet.

### get_blog

*Changes content*

Load one blog by UUID.

### get_design_guide

*Reads only*

Returns the guide to building a good NextPress page: page shape, words, colours and type, spacing, phone rules, pictures and links. Read it once before building a new page or section, and follow it.

### get_docs_guide

*Reads only*

The guide to writing good docs pages in NextPress, in plain words: one idea per page, a description on every page, Steps for tasks, Tabs and code groups for alternatives, callouts for warnings, diagrams for flows, and cards on overview pages. It ends with the MDX cheat sheet: the exact syntax of every component a page may use. Read it before you write or change a docs page. The write_docs prompt and the nextpress://docs/guide resource hold the same text.

### get_docs_tree

*Reads only*

Reads one docs' navigation: every page and group in sidebar order, each with its id, title, address, kind (page or group), whether it is hidden from the sidebar, its status, and the pages under it. Also returns the docs' header settings. Read it before you add, move or link pages, so you use ids and addresses that exist.

### get_page

*Changes content*

Load a page by UUID or slug including all its blocks (can be long). Note version for updates (expectedVersion). To work on the blocks, start with get_page_outline: it is much shorter.

### get_page_block

*Reads only*

Works on one saved page, or on a blog post when content_type is "post". Name it in "id". Here "id" is the page and "block_id" is the block. Returns one block in full as JSON: its content, styles, settings and children. Use it when the outline is not enough, for example to see the exact styles before changing them. Pass an id from get_page_outline. A very large block (many nested blocks) comes back without its children, which are listed as an outline instead; call get_page_block again on a child to read it.

### get_page_history

*Reads only*

Lists the earlier saved versions of a page, newest first, with the page's current version. Each entry has its version number, when it was saved, who saved it and how many blocks it held (not the blocks themselves). Use it to find a version to go back to after a bad change, then call restore_page_version. Accepts the page's UUID or slug.

### get_page_outline

*Reads only*

Works on one saved page, or on a blog post when content_type is "post". Name it in "id". Read this first. Returns a short outline of the whole page: one indented line per block with its name (no "core/", and change_page_blocks takes it that way too), its id, a custom label if it has one, and the key content (first words of text, heading level, button link, picture and alt text, stack type, header variant, popup slug, form field name). Use it to find the ids that get_page_block and change_page_blocks need, and read it again after anything changed the page. A line marked "← selected" is the block the person picked. Very large pages fold their deepest levels as "(+N inside)"; read those with get_page_block. It does not show styles or settings.

### get_post

*Changes content*

Load a post by UUID including all its blocks (can be long). Note version for updates. To work on the blocks, start with get_page_outline using content_type "post".

### get_site_context

*Changes content*

Site branding, active theme, settings, and health — start here before editing content.

### get_template

*Changes content*

Load one template including its block tree.

### get_template_part_usage

*Reads only*

Lists the pages that show a template part (drafts included, trashed pages not). Call it before changing or removing a part, because every page listed changes with it. Returns each page's id, title and status. A ready-made template (list_templates) is copied into pages, so it returns no pages.

### get_theme

*Changes content*

Load one theme, including colors and type. Use the id from list_themes or get_site_context.

### list_block_types

*Reads only*

Lists every block type you can add: name, label, kind (block = holds no other blocks, container = holds blocks), category, and a note on when to use it. Docs blocks are named docs/… and keep that prefix when you use them; a block that another group lists too shows "(also docs)". Use it to pick the right block for a section. For one block's fields and an example, call get_block_type.

### list_blogs

*Changes content*

Paginate blogs for this site. Use the id as blogId when creating posts.

### list_docs

*Reads only*

Lists this site's docs: each one's id (homeId), name, address, number of pages, whether search is on, and its status. A docs is a set of pages with its own header, sidebar and search. Use the id as homeId in the other docs tools. If the list is empty, make one with create_docs.

### list_form_submissions

*Reads only*

Reads what visitors sent through the site's Form blocks, newest first. Each answer has its form name, the page it came from, a status ("new" or "read") and its fields as label and value. The reply also lists every form name (to filter by) and how many answers are unread. Use it when the owner asks about leads, messages or sign-ups. It only reads: nothing is marked read or removed. Answers hold visitors' personal details, so quote only what the owner asked for.

### list_media

*Changes content*

Browse the media library. Each file has a url to use as an image block's url. Look here before using any picture, and never point images at other websites. If nothing fits, use /placeholder.png and tell the owner.

### list_pages

*Changes content*

Paginate pages (id, title, slug, status, version).

### list_posts

*Changes content*

Paginate blog posts.

### list_template_parts

*Reads only*

Lists this site's template parts: a header, footer or section designed once and shown on many pages. Each has its id, name, root block and usedOnPages (how many pages show it). Use it before building a header or footer, and reuse a part that exists instead of building the same thing again. To show one on a page, insert a core/template-part block with content \{"templateId": "&lt;id>"\} using change_page_blocks. A part is shared: changing it changes every page that uses it. (list_templates is different: those are ready-made blocks that get copied into a page.)

### list_templates

*Changes content*

List ready-made page/post templates: blocks that get copied into a page. For a shared header, footer or section that many pages show from one place, use list_template_parts instead.

### list_themes

*Changes content*

List installed themes (id, name, whether it is the active one).

### patch_page_blocks

*Changes content*

Will be removed in 0.4: use change_page_blocks. Apply insert/update/move/delete/replace ops to a page block tree with ready-made BlockConfig blocks. Requires expectedVersion from get_page. Kept for compatibility: prefer change_page_blocks, which takes simple block descriptions, fills in defaults, checks the page and needs no version number. Prefer either over a full update_page for edits. replace swaps a block and everything inside it for another block in the same spot.

### patch_post_blocks

*Changes content*

Will be removed in 0.4: use change_page_blocks with content_type "post". Apply insert/update/move/delete/replace ops to a post block tree with ready-made BlockConfig blocks. Requires expectedVersion from get_post.

### preview_page

*Changes content*

Create a time-limited share URL so humans can review a draft without logging in.

### preview_post

*Changes content*

Create a time-limited share URL so humans can review a draft post without logging in.

### publish_page

*Changes content*

Set page status to published. Requires expectedVersion from get_page. Prefer draft until the owner asks to publish.

### publish_post

*Changes content*

Set post status to published. Requires expectedVersion from get_post.

### read_docs_page

*Reads only*

Reads one docs page as MDX text, with its title, description, status and version. Send the version back as expectedVersion when you write the page. It also names any blocks that have no MDX form: writing the page drops them, so copy their content into the text first. Read the page again before every write.

### reorder_docs_pages

*Changes content*

Sets the order of the pages under one page or group, or at the top of the docs when parentId is left out. Send every page under that parent, each id once, in the new order (get the ids from get_docs_tree). If the list does not match the pages exactly, nothing moves and the reply says to read the tree again.

### restore_page_version

*Changes content*

Puts an earlier version of a page's blocks back. Send the version to go back to (from get_page_history) and expectedVersion, the page's current version from get_page_history or get_page. If the page has been saved since, nothing is restored and you are told to read it again, so you never undo someone else's newer work. The blocks being replaced are saved in the history first, so a restore can itself be undone. Only the blocks change, not the title, slug or status. Returns the page's new version and an outline of the restored blocks.

### update_docs_page

*Changes content*

Changes one docs page or group: its title, its address (the last part of its web address), the page or group it sits under, whether it is hidden from the sidebar, and whether it is a page or a group. Only the fields you send change. Changing an address breaks the links that point at the old one, so check them with get_docs_tree. The docs home stays at the top of the sidebar: it cannot be hidden, made a group or moved.

### update_docs_settings

*Changes content*

Changes one docs' header and frame: its name, logos, header links (up to six, in order), the button in the header, the search button, and the frame switches. Only the fields you send change. A list you send (links) replaces the old list, so send all of it. The reply gives the settings after the change.

### update_page

*Changes content*

Update page metadata (title, slug, status) or replace the whole block tree. Requires expectedVersion from get_page. On VERSION_STALE, re-get and retry. To change blocks, prefer change_page_blocks: it edits part of the page and checks the result.

### update_post

*Changes content*

Update a post's title, slug, excerpt or status, or replace its whole block tree. Requires expectedVersion from get_post. To change blocks, prefer change_page_blocks with content_type "post".

### update_theme

*Changes content*

Change a theme's name or design. The built-in Default theme cannot be edited.

### upload_media

*Changes content*

Upload a file from a local path (stdio host) or base64. Prefer path when the agent can read the filesystem.

### validate_blocks

*Changes content*

Will be removed in 0.4. Dry-run validate a BlockConfig[] against the NextPress registry (unknown names, structure). To check a page that is already saved, use check_page instead: it also covers the save rules and phone layout.

### write_docs_page

*Changes content*

Saves a docs page's MDX text as a new version. Read the page first with read_docs_page and send its version as expectedVersion. The text is checked as it is saved: if it has a mistake, nothing is saved and the reply names the line to fix. If the page changed somewhere else since you read it, nothing is saved and the reply tells you to read it again. Send the whole page each time. Blocks that read_docs_page names as having no MDX form are dropped by this save. Saving does not publish: the page stays a draft.
